emptyHint: Enter a domain and a backend address; the listener and site are set up in one go.
title: Quick site
domainHelp: The domain you type in the browser. It does not have to point at this device yet; the last step explains how to do that.
templates: Common apps (optional, fills in the port and recommended options)

tpl.homeassistant: Home Assistant needs use_x_forwarded_for: true under http in configuration.yaml, with the IP of the device running Gately in trusted_proxies; otherwise it returns 400.
tpl.jellyfin: The write timeout is extended for long playback. Add the device running Gately as a known proxy in Jellyfin's network settings so client IPs are correct.
tpl.emby: The write timeout is extended for long playback.
tpl.vaultwarden: The Vaultwarden web vault only works over HTTPS (browsers expose the crypto API only on secure connections), so choose HTTPS in the next step.
tpl.nextcloud: Upload and download idle timeouts are extended. Also add the domain to trusted_domains in Nextcloud's config.php and set overwriteprotocol to https when using HTTPS.
tpl.immich: Upload and download idle timeouts are extended for large video backups from phones.
tpl.proxmox: Proxmox VE uses a self-signed certificate by default, so Skip backend certificate verification is ticked. The console (noVNC) WebSocket is forwarded automatically.
tpl.synology: DSM's HTTPS port uses a self-signed certificate by default, so Skip backend certificate verification is ticked. You can also use http://host:5000.
tpl.fnos: The fnOS web UI listens on 5666 by default (5667 for HTTPS). Upload and download idle timeouts are extended.

targetHelp: Address of the service behind the proxy. Without a scheme, http is used, or https for port 443.
probeInsecure: The backend uses a self-signed certificate; certificate verification will be skipped.

reason.refused: Connection refused: nothing is listening on that port. Check the port and that the service is running
reason.timeout: Timed out: check the address and the firewall
reason.dns: The host name cannot be resolved
reason.protocol: Protocol mismatch: try https instead of http, or the other way round

skipVerify: Skip backend certificate verification (needed for self-signed certificates)
wsHint: WebSocket is forwarded automatically, nothing to set up.
httpsHelp: Recommended. An existing certificate for the domain is used; otherwise request one below.
httpHelp: Unencrypted; fine on a LAN or for a quick test.
sslOff: The certificate module is off, so only HTTP is available. Turn it on under Settings → Modules.
planRedirect: A new HTTPS listener on port {port} is created, and port 80 redirects HTTP requests to HTTPS.
planPlain: A new listener on port {port} is created.
certNone: No certificate covers {domain} yet. Pick a validation method and it is requested in the background.
emailHelp: The CA uses it for notices such as certificate expiry.
listenerGone: The selected listener no longer exists. Refresh and try again
certPending: The certificate is being requested in the background; until it is issued, HTTPS visits show a certificate error.
dnsTitle: The domain does not point at this device yet?
dnsRecord: Add an A (IPv4) or AAAA (IPv6) record at your DNS provider pointing at this device's public IP, and forward the port on your router to this device.
dnsDynamic: If your home IP changes, let dynamic DNS keep the record up to date.
dnsHosts: Just testing locally: add a line with this device's IP and {domain} to your computer's hosts file.
